title: Subnet News — October 14, 2026
summary: Bittensor halves subnet immunity and accelerates registration-cost decay. SN65 TPN publishes its model evidence, SN46 Instant joins Liquid Inference, SN55 NIOME reports its completed synthetic CRISPR run, and SN10 Pareton opens a Kimi K3 optimization campaign. Also: cross-subnet integrations, miner reward and reliability changes, Const’s SN92 correction and today’s SN48 Quantum Compute interview. Coverage through October 14 at 11:02 AM Eastern.

updates.headline: SN7 allways changes capacity rewards and repairs validator startup
updates.summary: SN7 allways’ merge makes the capacity ramp linear and raises the qualified-volume portion of each lane pool from 25% to 35%. The same release addresses a repeated bond-relay vault walk that its incident notes say could stall validator boot for roughly300 seconds. A separate merge excludes unusable-address quotes from scoring for12 rounds. These changes alter how miners earn and reduce a documented startup failure path. Public code is verified; actual adoption by every validator and future returns are not.
updates.ratingReason: Specific reward changes and an operational repair affect miner competition and validator availability.

updates.headline: SN10 Pareton announces a live Kimi K3 optimization campaign
updates.summary: SN10 Pareton’s October 14 announcement asks miners to accelerate Kimi K3 on SGLang using eight B300 GPUs and16 concurrent requests while preserving model quality. Its merged campaign fixture provides a primary implementation trail. The opportunity is workload-specific inference optimization, not a newly measured speedup or a claim that every customer already receives cheaper inference. The general landing page still includes a Coming Soon label, so this report attributes the live-campaign status to the official announcement rather than claiming a completed end-to-end miner submission test. A separate RTX5090 purchase post describes planned capacity expansion, not GPUs already serving customers.
updates.ratingReason: A specific announced campaign and implementation give miners an actionable new optimization target.

updates.headline: SN15 ORO updates task-pack compatibility and the runtime contract
updates.summary: SN15 ORO’s merged release moves to oro-env-runtime3.7.0 and contract5, using a shared reader for both v7 andv8 task packs. It corrects a preflight startup failure when a v8 pack begins with an encoding record, and refreshes practice delivery and checks. The bundled practice set keeps the same30 tasks and grading. This matters to miners preparing submissions because a packaging mismatch should not masquerade as model failure; it is not a new benchmark win.
updates.ratingReason: A verified task-loading and runtime compatibility update prevents a concrete startup failure.

updates.headline: SN21 AdTAO adds an optional champion what-if forecasting relay
updates.summary: SN21 AdTAO’s code adds read-only forecasts from the current champion for what-if episodes, running under the daily sandbox and limits with a 75 second wall clock. It is off unless SN21_FORECAST_RELAY=1 and does not write those episodes into the scoring ledger. Another model-privacy state machine is expressly not wired into publication. This is a specific implementation step toward interactive campaign scenarios, not a confirmed public feature rollout or a promise of additional ad conversions.
updates.ratingReason: An optional implementation connects champion models to scenario forecasts while protecting scoring state.

updates.headline: SN37 Aurelius publishes a disabled stake-retention design
updates.summary: SN37 Aurelius’ new incentives document describes a planned holding-time mechanism: retained stake builds credit, transferred-in stake earns no credit, and exits can incur penalties and debt. The document explicitly says the mechanism is currently disabled and details will be published before activation. Separate miner tooling adds an incentive-terms acknowledgement. This is useful advance notice for operators deciding how to participate; it must not be presented as an already enforced lock or a guaranteed reward boost.

updates.headline: SN51 Lium protects rental hosts from memory exhaustion
updates.summary: SN51 Lium’s merged rental fix reserves host memory, caps each rental’s share, disables container swap and gives renter processes a higher out-of-memory priority. The incident notes describe an8×H200 rental consuming99.7% of guest RAM and starving the agent/executor for25 hours. Another fix isolates DNS lookups with a 15 second deadline and miner-scoped quotas so one stalled miner cannot monopolize resolution. These are concrete safeguards for availability, not evidence that every prior rental issue is resolved or a new monthly revenue result.
updates.ratingReason: Primary incident notes and repairs address long-running rental and validator failure modes.

updates.headline: SN55 NIOME reports completion of ten million synthetic CRISPR experiments
updates.summary: SN55 NIOME’s October 14 post reports completion of its synthetic CRISPR run and a transition toward pharmacogenomics, predicting drug response. Its post and inspected artwork explicitly describe synthetic experiments, not procedures performed on patients; the team says no real patient records were involved. It reports 248 miners across 256 slots, nine validators and723 tasks processed alongside the ten-million total. Those are distinct counts, not ten million independently audited clinical successes. This matters as a completed network workload and a clearly stated next research focus, while model utility and biological validity still require separate evidence.
updates.ratingReason: A completed, named synthetic workload is a substantive milestone with clear boundaries around clinical interpretation.

updates.headline: SN65 TPN publishes the evidence behind TPN-005
updates.summary: SN65 TPN’s October 14 case study adds concrete evidence to its October 12 model announcement. The K11 run record lists a 7.24 GB artifact, 10.98 GiB of measured RAM under an 11 GiB ceiling, and 73.93% on 1,400 fluid_knowledge items versus the F16 reference’s 66.57%. The file is 57.4% smaller than the 16.99 GB reference and the score is 7.36 percentage points higher. The study attributes the gain to capability-directed tuning as well as compression. Both linked records use the same sealed epoch and manifest; their recorded evaluation context is 8,192 tokens, so the model’s wider context capability is not a benchmark of that full window. These are published team results, not an independent rerun or a universal reasoning advantage. The new value is traceable evidence of meeting a specific memory-and-knowledge target.
updates.ratingReason: A dated detailed case study and matching public run records substantiate a useful constrained-model result.

updates.headline: SN66 Conjectures extends chat-log requirements to every open proof target
updates.summary: SN66 Conjectures’ merged October 13 policy requires the AI chat logs used to produce a proof for every open target, including submissions through the coldkey-signed CLI. The code checks linked-account logs after signature verification and refuses a missing-log submission before spending its payment. New-target terms also describe a 2.5% starting treasury share ramping to 12.5% over15 days and earlier-proof bonus provisions. This changes both evidence obligations and reward expectations; accepted submissions retain their recorded policy. Production publication settings are separately gated, so merged terms are not proof that every deployment has adopted them.
updates.ratingReason: Verified submission and bounty-policy changes materially affect proof contributors.

updates.headline: SN81 Reliquary fixes a duplicate-answer cursor deadlock
updates.summary: SN81 Reliquary’s merged correction lets a corpus walk advance without payment when a submission repeats its own completion. Previously a prompt that naturally elicited only one answer could trap a miner indefinitely because admission rejected the duplicate before moving its cursor. Copying earlier work still does not earn advancement under this exception. This is a focused availability repair, separate from the earlier holdout scoring changes; deployment across the fleet was not independently checked.
updates.ratingReason: A reproduced class of permanently blocked miner jobs receives a targeted implementation fix.

sources.label: SN81 primary implementation and release notes

updates.headline: SN89 InfiniteQuant raises its Markets entity dust floor after a pruning incident
updates.summary: SN89 InfiniteQuant’s October 14 commit says a collateral-holding Markets entity was pruned from UID199 around04:36UTC because its dust allocation sat below immune low/high-frequency miners. The change schedules a vault-UID floor inside the Markets vector from 13:00UTC, while retaining earlier-cycle behavior for historical replay. This is a concrete protective correction to the new Markets mechanism, not proof that pruning is reversed or every claimant is paid. The reported pruning details come from the primary incident note; the particular event was not separately reconstructed on-chain.
updates.ratingReason: A documented pruning failure leads to an explicit reward-floor repair for collateral-holding entities.

updates.summary: In a directly reviewed October 14 reply, Const answers “No not me” to a bot asking whether he owns SN92. The bot’s launch label and the slot’s roughly293.90%24 hour alpha/TAO rise do not establish current team identity or a new registration. Direct node endpoint comparisons show no registration-height or owner change between yesterday’s cutoff and block9,282,237; that comparison cannot exclude every intervening event or an off-chain deal. The verified news here is the denial, not an endorsement, ownership claim or negotiated sale.

ecosystem.headline: Bittensor halves subnet immunity and speeds up registration-cost decay
ecosystem.summary: Direct finalized node reads show NetworkImmunityPeriod falling from 864,000 to 432,000 blocks and NetworkLockReductionInterval from 115,200 to 57,600 blocks between blocks 9,275,607 and 9,282,237. At an assumed 12 seconds per block, those correspond to roughly 120→60 days of immunity and 16→8 days for the lock-reduction interval; calendar timing depends on block production. NetworkMinLockCost remains 1 TAO. This gives new teams less protected time to establish their subnet and makes registration costs decline faster. It is an observed active parameter change, not merely a proposal; it does not identify a newly deregistered slot or prove any particular sale.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Active protocol parameters change the protection period and entry-cost dynamics for subnet operators.

Finalized block reference; parameter values queried directly on archive RPC
